title: The Lamb Chased by a Wolf
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Wolf was chasing a Lamb, which took refuge in a temple. The Wolf urged it to come out of the precincts, and said, "If you don't, the priest is sure to catch you and offer you up in sacrifice on the altar." To which the Lamb replied, "Thanks, I think I'll stay where I am: I'd rather be sacrificed any day than be eaten up by a Wolf."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Wolf doing to the Lamb at the start of the fable?
options: Teaching her to hunt
Leading her to a temple to worship
Chasing her
Guarding her from other wolves

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Lamb take refuge from the Wolf?
options: In a temple
Up a tree
Behind a rock
Inside a cave

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf urge the Lamb to do?
options: Pray to the priest for mercy
Hide deeper inside the temple
Wait until nightfall
Come out of the precincts

questions.prompt: According to the Wolf, what will the priest do to the Lamb if she does not come out?
options: Feed her and set her free
Catch her and offer her up in sacrifice on the altar
Chase her back toward the Wolf
Keep her in the temple forever

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "precincts" mean in "come out of the precincts"?
options: The priests who serve the temple
The songs sung inside the temple
The grounds or enclosed area of the temple
The road leading away from the temple

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "refuge" mean in "took refuge in a temple"?
options: A shelter or safety from danger
A place of worship for wolves
A punishment for wrongdoing
A gathering of priests

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Lamb doubt that the Wolf's warning about the priest is meant to help her?
options: The Wolf has never met the priest and cannot know his plans
The temple has no priest at all, so the warning must be false
The Lamb cannot hear the Wolf clearly from inside the temple
The Wolf itself stands to eat her if she comes out, so its warning serves its own interest

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Temples always offer complete safety from predators
Faced with death either way, the Lamb prefers the fate that does not satisfy her enemy
Priests are more dangerous than wolves
The Lamb trusts the Wolf's advice because it comes from concern for her safety

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what are the exact opening words of the Lamb's reply?
options: "No, thank you, I am quite safe here"
"Never, I would sooner starve"
"Thanks, I think I'll stay where I am"
"Go away and leave me be"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Lamb say she would rather be?
options: Forgiven
Hidden
Adopted
Sacrificed

questions.prompt: According to the Lamb, what fate does she prefer to being eaten by a Wolf?
options: Being sold to a farmer
Being sacrificed
Being chased forever
Being kept as a pet

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "sacrificed" mean in "rather be sacrificed any day"?
options: Ritually killed as an offering
Set free by the priest
Cured of an illness
Praised in a ceremony

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Lamb's answer reveal about how she weighs her two possible fates?
options: She believes the priest will surely spare her once she explains herself
She thinks the Wolf will lose interest if she waits long enough
She does not realize either fate involves death
She sees both fates as certain death, but prefers not to give the Wolf its meal

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Wolf and a Lamb make peace inside a temple
A priest rescues a Lamb from a Wolf and keeps her at the temple
A Wolf chases a Lamb into a temple and warns her the priest will sacrifice her, but she chooses to stay rather than risk being eaten by the Wolf
A Lamb tricks a Wolf into entering the temple in her place
